examples: Let a second computer run Claude sessions on one of your Claude accounts without logging it in there.
See, per account and computer, whether the access token was last pushed, failed, or was refused.
On the receiving computer, make a relayed Claude account the default for new sessions so a plain new session needs no login.
On the receiving computer, start a Codex session on a relayed Codex account and restart it later on the same login.
how_to: On by default for every account: an account the owner has not switched off is sent to every paired computer whose own owner allows receiving credentials. The owner can switch an account off in the app (pack, logins tab, credential relay).
Only the computer that owns the login ever refreshes it; the other computers receive a fresh access token and its expiry, never the refresh token.

A receiving computer keeps the copy in its own relay profile, never in a login someone made there, and receives it only after its own owner turns on may receive credentials (off by default; this did not change).

The receiving computer's owner accepts logins per account: all of them, only a named list, or none. Until it answers, nothing is written there; an account offered later under a named list waits as pending. Owner only, no mcp tool.

A popup in the middle of the screen asks for that answer the first time a paired computer offers a login: yes or no, with no way to dismiss it, and a checklist of the offered accounts (all ticked) plus an all accounts box that also covers accounts added later. Change it any time under pack, logins, this computer receives.
Codex logins relay the same way, as an access-only copy on their own route; Carnivore never refreshes a Codex login, so the copy lapses with the owner's own codex refresh.

A relayed login appears on the receiving computer's providers page as a card tagged relayed, with the time its access copy lasts. The receiving computer never refreshes it, polls it or runs the keep-fresh step on it: the owner's computer renews the copy. Press the switch button on that card to make it the default for new sessions; the new session, restart and recreate pickers list it too, and each launches on the relay profile. The mcp tool pack_relay_account_use does the same switch.

A relayed Codex login works the same way on the receiving computer: it is listed on the providers page as relayed, offered in the new session, restart, recreate and wake pickers for Codex sessions, and can be made the default for new Codex sessions. Its sessions run on their own Codex home, with token refresh and revoke pointed at a dead address, and auto switch never moves it.
media_exempt: The popup and the logins block need a paired computer that offers a login, which a leased test slot does not have; no capture is defined yet.
name: Pack credential relay
summary: the computer that owns a Claude login copies its fresh access token, never the refresh token, to the Pack computers you pick, so they can run that account without a login of their own.
where: Pack, logins tab: the credential relay block and the this computer receives block; the allow logins popup; the providers page (relayed cards); the mcp tools pack_relay_status and pack_relay_account_use.
